headline: UMaine says FY28 budget gap will require layoffs and faculty retrenchments
dek: The university says a projected $19 million structural shortfall is forcing personnel reductions, though details and timing are still being developed.
body: The University of Maine says it will need strategic staff layoffs and faculty retrenchments as it prepares an FY28 budget facing a projected $19 million structural gap. President Joan Ferrini-Mundy announced the decision in a Sept. 17 message to employees.

The university said operating costs have grown faster than state support and tuition revenue, while enrollment pressure and changes to federal research funding and financial aid have added uncertainty. Leaders said reserves and one-time savings have largely been used to limit the effect on positions in earlier budget cycles.

Academic Affairs, which the university said represents about half of UMaine’s budget, has committed to reducing its FY28 base expenses by $10 million. The plan includes permanently eliminating about one-fifth of vacant positions, reducing overload teaching and other instructional budgets, and consolidating some course sections.

UMaine said the remaining $5.7 million gap in Academic Affairs could require additional layoffs and faculty retrenchments if other savings or new revenue do not materialize. More proposals are still being developed across the university, with a budget town hall planned for October.
author: NorthEast News Desk
sourceName: University of Maine Office of the President
